Title: Otters offer hope for Klang River's recovery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Beneath a tangle of highways in the capital, a family of otters rolls around in a patch of riverside sand, delighting the few passersby who notice them.
Small groups of otters are now seen regularly in parts of the city, including along the once heavily polluted Klang River.
Theories vary on whether the smooth-coated otters, classed as vulnerable by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, have returned to the city or were hiding in plain sight all along.
However, their presence has raised hopes that efforts to clean up the Klang are bearing fruit and could inspire further improvement.
The Klang River was once one of the world's dirtiest waterways, designated a Class 5, severely polluted river under Malaysia's rankings.
Years of work improved it to Class 3, or moderately polluted, which seems to have encouraged the otters to move in, said Malaysian wildlife ecologist Woo Chee Yoong.
"Wherever there are otters, there are fish. Wherever there are fish, it means the whole river system... (is) clean; it's healthy for all the communities around. So that's one of the importance of otters," he said.
In recent years, the animals have been filmed sunbathing on the river's concrete banks and swimming in front of elevated metro stations, winning viral fame.
[[nid:1583722]]
Retired soldier Hasan Ujang, who lives in a riverside apartment, enjoys watching their antics.
"We feel really happy when we watch them playing and playing, like kids swimming," he said.
But unlike otters in neighbouring Singapore, which are closely monitored by a network of citizen scientists, little is known about Kuala Lumpur's otters.
Woo learned about them from local media reports on sightings in 2019 and co-founded the Malaysian Otter Network (MON) conservation group the following year.
"We don't know how many groups are there; we don't know how the otters are actually moving around," he said.
Even the question of whether the otters have returned to the capital or were simply in less visible city environments before remains a "mystery."
MON hopes to set up a citizen science system for people to report sightings.
Otters have been spotted elsewhere in the city, including at the Tropicana Golf & Country Resort, a high-end housing estate where they are less welcome visitors.
They are accused of raiding fish ponds at at least 12 houses in the past year.
Resident Yee Sze Mun, 89, said otters killed the beloved – and expensive – arowana fish he had nurtured for 15 years.
"They are a nuisance, but I can't blame them, because they are just like us; they have to survive," he said.
Residents say the incursions began last year after a company began clearing forest next door for a new development.
"We have an issue because they're losing their habitat," said residents' association president Joy Appukuttan, who called the otter attacks a "grave concern."
Tropicana's security team believes there are around 25 otters in the forest, and the estate brought in Woo to teach residents how to deal with them.
The species is protected in Malaysia, so Woo urges residents to block entry points to their yards and install fences or netting over ponds.
Former Kuala Lumpur mayor and current city adviser on sustainable urbanisation Maimunah Mohd Sharif called the otters an asset.
"Otters are one of the benchmarks for clean cities," she said.
Like others, she hopes a growing awareness of the Klang River otters can be harnessed to help improve the river further.
Hundreds of garbage traps were installed under the government's River of Life project, while solar-powered interceptors deployed by a Dutch NGO have collected tens of thousands of tonnes of waste.
Maimunah now wants more done to stop waste from entering the river in the first place, alongside efforts to elevate the Klang to Class 2B status — clean enough for body contact.
"One day, I want to swim in the Klang River," she said.
Scarlett Koon Si Qi, a community architect and co-organiser of the annual Klang River Festival, hopes the waterway can be restored to its natural banks without concrete lining.
"Some parts, maybe yes, you do need concrete to kind of protect and control for floods," she said.
"But I think wherever we can, we should leave it as natural as possible."
That would further benefit the otters, who need some vegetation and natural crevices to hide in, experts said.
The otters are already shifting views on the river, said Faith Foo, who runs the festival.
Growing up, "the teachers would always say that this is a very unsanitary place," he said.
But seeing the otters, "it's a reminder that it is a river."--AFP

Title: Parents put work aside to support children sitting SPM
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Parents are taking time off work to accompany their children through the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examinations, putting aside their own nerves to offer support on the first day of the written papers today.
Faizul Jasman, 46, said he had taken leave to be with his eldest son.
"I think our son needs us, at least on the first day. And for the rest of the days, I have to teach him to be independent.
"At least on the first day, he knows his mum and dad are always there to support him," he said when met at SMK Putrajaya Presint 16(1).
The father of five said his son had been coping well with the examinations, with the family beginning preparations a week earlier by ensuring he got enough sleep and giving him space to focus.
He credited the teachers for keeping students on track.
"They have been (supporting) non-stop. Whenever there's a gap, they hold extra classes, they hold tuition," he said.
Faizul said that when his son felt burnt out from daily classes, which sometimes extended into weekends, he and his wife would take him out for meals and let him choose what he wanted.
However, they continued to limit his phone use and keep track of his friends.
He said the family would focus on his son's results before helping him plan his next step.
"We'll look at his performance first.
"After that, it'll probably mostly be about letting him cool down, and then bringing him back to look at what he wants in the future.
"His journey doesn't end at SPM. He has a much better future ahead," he said.
Meanwhile, Suryana Bakar, 48, said her nervousness stemmed from how relaxed her son, an economics stream student, appeared compared with his older sister when she sat the examination.
"With his older sister, you could see her preparing. With my son, he just seems relaxed.
"My heart is pounding, I'm actually nervous because I'm worried. He's not like his older sister," she said.
Suryana said learning methods today were too different for her to guide him directly, so she relied on his teachers, tuition classes and his older sister to help him prepare.
She said she did not put too much pressure on him, instead relying on a mix of reminders and encouragement.
"I'm not the type to force him. However much you study, that's the result you'll get.
"I just hope that this time, for the actual exam, he'll do even better than he did in the trials," she said.
For the first time, the Bahasa Melayu and English listening tests are being held
on the same day
as their respective Papers 1 and 2, instead of being scheduled separately as in previous years.

Title: Mother takes SPM to encourage autistic son in Kelantan
Article:
KOTA BARU:  A mother is sitting the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination as a private candidate to encourage her autistic son, who is taking the same examination.
Muhammad Adam Daniel Othman, 17, and his mother, Mazlina Abdul Majid, 44, attended the same examination centre at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Kota Baru for the first day of the written examination, although they were assigned to different examination halls.
Mazlina is sitting for six subjects.
Mazlina, a dental surgery assistant at the Kota Baru Dental Clinic, said she decided to take the examination to accompany her eldest son, whom she felt was losing motivation.
"Adam was diagnosed with autism two years ago. He often told me he had lost the motivation to sit for the SPM examination and felt like giving up.
"I decided to register as a private candidate and sit the examination at the same centre as Adam to encourage him.
"I also wanted to improve my previous SPM results, which could help me secure a higher job grade if I obtain good results," she said when met at the school today.
Mazlina said she received permission from her department to sit the examination in May and immediately began studying through YouTube. She also hired a private tutor for Mathematics.
"I study and revise at night, mostly with Adam, to encourage him.
"Now I am the one feeling nervous, but I cannot hide how proud I am to be here with my son, even though we are not sitting in the same examination hall," she said.
Adam said he felt relieved to have his mother with him when he lacked motivation and struggled to understand his lessons.
The eldest of four siblings said he would do his best and hoped they would both achieve good results.
"Studying is difficult, but having my mother by my side and revising together makes me feel relieved. I will do my best," he said.

Title: RM2.87mil meth haul uncovered in vape cartridges, Chinese tea packets
Article:
SEPANG: The Customs Department seized methamphetamine worth more than RM2.87 million in two separate operations at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Free Trade Zone on Nov 4 and 14.
KLIA Customs director Aspalila Ag Tuah said the first seizure, on Nov 14, involved 15,456 vape cartridges containing 30.91 litres of liquid suspected to be methamphetamine, worth an estimated RM1.54 million.
Initial investigations found that the cartridges had been brought in from Kuching, Sarawak, using Customs declaration forms.
"The syndicate attempted to evade detection by using cargo delivery services to transport the drugs and converting them into liquid form in vape cartridges," she said in a statement today.
In the second case, Customs intercepted two boxes registered for export to a country in Oceania through a cargo terminal operator.
The inspection uncovered 26 compressed crystal blocks of methamphetamine weighing 26.55kg and worth an estimated RM1.32 million.
"The drugs were concealed in plastic packets labelled 'Refined Chinese Tea' and sent through a parcel service in an attempt to evade detection during screening," she said.
Following the seizures, representatives of the companies handling the shipments were called in to assist investigations.
Both cases are being investigated under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. Conviction carries the death penalty or life imprisonment and not fewer than 12 strokes of the rotan.
Those with information on smuggling activities can contact the Customs toll-free hotline at 1-800-88-8855 or the nearest Customs office. The department said informants' identities would be kept confidential.

Title: RM780,000 sought to repair streetlights damaged by cable theft in Putrajaya
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A RM780,000 funding application to repair streetlights affected by cable theft along Federal Routes FT29 and FT30 in Putrajaya has been deferred to a subsequent phase of implementation.
Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan said the application was submitted in March this year, but implementation would depend on the ministry's funding priorities.
"The road safety infrastructure upgrading programme prioritises small-scale, targeted streetlight installations at accident-prone locations or areas posing risks to motorists due to poor lighting," he told the Dewan Rakyat.
He was responding to a question from Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin (Bersatu-Putrajaya) on the maintenance of streetlights and road markings along FT29 and FT30, including the use of solar-powered streetlights in areas frequently affected by cable theft.
Ahmad said priority would be given to high-risk locations such as junctions, bends and bridges, based on accident records and lighting requirements.
He said the Works Ministry allocated RM840,000 in 2025 under the Peninsular Malaysia Federal Road Maintenance Programme for seven streetlight maintenance projects.
"The works have been completed along several routes around Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), FT29 and FT30, including the slip roads at Persiaran APEC, Putrajaya Sentral, the National Cancer Institute and Persiaran Selatan," he said.
Ahmad said road marking works along both directions of FT30, costing RM1 million, were completed on Oct 31.
He said the project, carried out under Phase Two of the Non-Routine Pavement Maintenance Programme, began on Aug 12 this year to improve road safety.

Title: Construction, tech stocks lead Bursa losses as Trump's data centre threat rattles investors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Construction and technology stocks bore the brunt of selling pressure on Bursa Malaysia on Monday, as US President Donald Trump's threat to penalise American companies building data centres overseas rattled investor confidence in the sector's global growth prospects.
The construction index fell 3.15 per cent, making it the market's worst-performing sector, followed by technology, which shed 2.86 per cent, as investors reacted to US President Donald Trump's threat to impose a "tremendous tax" on American companies building data centres overseas, raising concerns over the industry's global expansion prospects.
At 10.50am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 8.46 points, or 0.54 per cent, to 1,548.24, with selling pressure extending across the broader market.
Real estate investment trusts (REITs) declined 16.89 points, or 1.95 per cent, while healthcare shed 35.05 points, or 2.31 per cent.
Utilities fell 31.36 points, or 1.94 per cent, industrial products and services declined 3.37 points, or 2.10 per cent, while energy lost 11.20 points, or 1.51 per cent.
Among the top losers, Kelington Group Bhd fell 64 sen, or 9.37 per cent, to RM6.19 from its opening price of RM6.83.
KLCC Property Holdings Bhd and KLCC REIT dropped 50 sen, or 5.63 per cent, to RM8.38, while Sunway Construction Group Bhd declined 44 sen, or 6.36 per cent, to RM6.48.
Vitrox Corp Bhd fell 39 sen, or 4.47 per cent, to RM8.33, while Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd lost 36 sen, or 1.82 per cent, to RM19.40.
Among actively traded counters, VS Industry Bhd, with a trading volume of 11.94 million shares, fell one sen, or 4.08 per cent, to 23.5 sen after opening at 24 sen.
Dagang Nexchange Bhd declined 1.5 sen, or 3.57 per cent, to 40.5 sen after opening at 41.5 sen.
Trump's remarks have added to uncertainty surrounding the data centre sector, which has already faced pressure from tighter US restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to several Southeast Asian countries, including Malaysia.
He contrasted his push to keep AI infrastructure in the US with foreign production of advanced computer chips, which he said had been "very destructive to our country".
The latest weakness extends the FBM KLCI's downward trend, following five consecutive trading days of losses earlier this month and a decline of 53.27 points, or 3.26 per cent, between Nov 5 and Nov 14.
The benchmark has since struggled to regain the 1,600-point level, with foreign fund outflows, global technology weakness and concerns over AI-related capital expenditure continuing to weigh on sentiment.

Title: 13 Johor water treatment plants at risk amid Super El Nino
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Thirteen water treatment plants (LRA) across five districts in Johor have been identified as at risk of raw water shortages amid projections of a Super El Nino phenomenon lasting until early next year.
State Works, Transportation, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh said the five districts were Johor Baru, Kota Tinggi, Kulai, Kluang and Segamat.
He said these areas would be prioritised in preparedness measures to ensure uninterrupted water supply to consumers.
Fazli said the Johor government had submitted an application to the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), in collaboration with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), to carry out cloud seeding operations from November 2026 to June 2027.
He said the operations were aimed at boosting rainfall in water catchment areas before dam levels and raw water sources experienced more serious depletion.
He said this during the second meeting of the first term of the 16th Johor State Legislative Assembly (DUN) in Kota Iskandar here today, in reply to a question from Bentayan assemblyman Ng Yak Howe on the state government's preparations for the phenomenon.
Fazli said that based on MetMalaysia projections, the El Nino phenomenon could reach a very strong or Super El Nino level between November 2026 and part of January 2027 before weakening gradually in May to June next year.
However, he said the more concerning period was from late January to mid-March 2027, when monsoon rainfall was expected to drop significantly, raising the risk of hot weather and prolonged drought.
He said the state government had held drought preparedness meetings on Oct 26 and Nov 3 with relevant agencies, including Johor MetMalaysia, the Johor Water Regulatory Body and Ranhill SAJ, to strengthen early readiness.
"The state government will utilise the northeast monsoon period to step up preparedness before the risk of hot weather and drought becomes more pronounced," he said.
He said identified mitigation measures included the Seluyut-Layang raw water transfer with a capacity of up to 300 million litres per day, water transfers from the Seluyut Dam to the Lebam Dam, and supplementary pumping to support water sources at the Machap Dam, Sembrong Dam and Lok Heng LRA.
Daily monitoring of dam, river and LRA intake levels was also being conducted by the water regulatory body, the Drainage and Irrigation Department and Ranhill SAJ to enable early mitigation action, he said.
He added that alternative water sources from former mining ponds, lakes and quarries in Layang-Layang, Gunung Pulai, Sayong and Sembrong had also been identified, subject to technical suitability and water quality test results.

Title: New investment framework to protect local industries from tax breaks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government hopes its new investment incentive framework will prevent tax exemptions granted to foreign companies from undermining local industries, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said.
He said the New Incentive Framework (NIF), introduced on March 1, requires investment proposals to undergo a six-part assessment before companies can qualify for incentives.
"Under the NIF, all investments must go through a scorecard assessment.
"Incentives will only be granted to investments that achieve the required scores, including criteria relating to economic complexity and the employment of more local workers," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
Liew was responding to a supplementary question from Lim Guan Eng (PH-Bagan), who raised concerns over the impact of long-term tax holidays granted to foreign companies, particularly in the steel industry.
Lim claimed that foreign steel manufacturers had benefited from tax exemptions lasting up to 15 years, allowing them to avoid paying the standard 24 per cent corporate tax rate.
He alleged that the incentives had placed Malaysian steel producers at a disadvantage.
"In 2016, Malaysian companies controlled 85 per cent of the steel industry. Now, 85 per cent is controlled by foreign companies," he said.
Lim also claimed that MA Steel was the only remaining local steel company and questioned how long it could survive under the present conditions.
He urged the government to review tax holidays to ensure that investment incentives did not come at the expense of domestic industries.
Lim said local companies should also be able to benefit from such incentives to remain competitive and expand their businesses.
In response, Liew said the NIF was designed to address such concerns by linking incentives to measurable economic contributions.
He expressed hope that the framework would prevent a repeat of the situation raised by Lim.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dewan Rakyat observes moment of silence for former Dewan Negara deputy president
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Rakyat today observed a moment of silence in honour of former Dewan Negara deputy president Datuk Seri Abdul Halim Abd Samad, who died yesterday.
Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul announced Abdul Halim's death at the start of proceedings and conveyed Parliament's condolences to his family.
"It is with deep sadness that I inform the House of the passing of former Dewan Negara deputy president Datuk Seri Abdul Halim Abd Samad on Nov 22.
"On behalf of all members of this House and Parliament, I extend our deepest condolences to his family.
"May his family be given strength during this difficult time," he said.
Johari then invited Muslim members of parliament to recite al-Fatihah and non-Muslim MPs to observe a moment of silence in remembrance of Abdul Halim.
He also prayed for Abdul Halim's soul to be blessed and for him to be placed among the righteous.
Abdul Halim, 86, died from a lung infection.
He was appointed as senator on Nov 3, 2014, and served as Dewan Negara deputy president from April 18, 2016, to Nov 2, 2020.

Title: Grieving father's death, injured SPM candidate determined to sit exams in wheelchair
Article:
PONTIAN: Despite being offered medical leave and the option of sitting the 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examinations in hospital, Syasya Nasuha Zainal, 17, was determined to attend school today.
The student from SMK Dato' Penggawa Barat here had to use a wheelchair on the first day of the examinations after injuring her right ankle in a fall during an activity at Stadium Pontian last Saturday.
Her ankle was swollen, leaving her unable to walk.
The eldest of two siblings remained determined to sit the Bahasa Melayu paper, accompanied by her mother, Mirul Fathiah Mustapha, 44.
"If I had wanted to, I could have taken medical leave and sat the SPM examination in hospital. However, I told the doctor and my mother that I could come to school today with my friends.
"I am happy to be able to come to school and hope to answer the questions well," she said when met during a visit by Johor Education director Zulkurnain Abdul Rahman to the school.
Syasya said her biggest challenge was losing her father, Zainal Hasbullah, 44, who died on Sept 15 from complications arising from kidney disease.
"Losing my father so close to the examinations has deeply affected me, as he was the one who always encouraged me to achieve excellent results. I had already proved myself in the trial examinations, and I intend to do the same in the SPM, which begins today," she said.
Meanwhile, Mirul Fathiah said she was proud that her eldest daughter remained determined to study and sit the SPM despite losing her father and suffering an injury that left her ankle swollen.

Title: Malaysia to collect global minimum tax revenue only after June 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will only begin collecting revenue from the global minimum tax (GMT) after June 2027, despite having implemented the tax in January last year.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the collection timeline was determined by financial reporting requirements for multinational companies subject to the 15 per cent minimum effective tax rate.
"Malaysia implemented the GMT on Jan 1, 2025, in line with its commitment under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development's (OECD) Base Erosion and Profit Shifting framework.
"However, tax revenue under the GMT will only be collected after June 2027, based on the financial reporting periods of multinational groups subject to the top-up tax," he told the Dewan Rakyat.
Liew said affected companies had 18 months after the end of their financial reporting period to submit their returns and pay the additional tax.
He was responding to Lim Guan Eng (PH-Bagan), who asked how much revenue Malaysia had collected from the GMT since its implementation in 2025.
He also asked whether the government would reduce the tax rate for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to 15 per cent to ensure fairer treatment compared with multinational companies.
Liew said the GMT was introduced to address profit shifting by multinational companies to jurisdictions offering low or zero corporate tax rates.
"The implementation of the GMT is expected to have a positive impact on the country's financial position," he said.
Liew said more than 135 countries and jurisdictions had agreed in October 2021 to implement the GMT under the OECD Inclusive Framework on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting.
Implementation began in stages internationally in 2024, with about 65 countries and jurisdictions having introduced the rules as of October this year.
On tax relief for MSMEs, Liew said the 2027 Budget proposed a one-percentage-point reduction in income tax rates from the 2027 assessment year.
The rate on the first RM150,000 of chargeable income will fall from 15 to 14 per cent, while the rate on income between RM150,001 and RM600,000 will be reduced from 17 to 16 per cent.
He said the reductions could save eligible businesses up to RM6,000 in taxes, helping to ease operating costs and improve cash flow.

Title: Trump's overseas data centre threat raises fresh risks for Malaysian contractors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: US President Donald Trump's proposed restrictions on American companies building data centres overseas could delay new construction contract awards in Malaysia, raising fresh uncertainty for contractors banking on the country's booming data centre investment pipeline.
RHB Research warned that the proposal could trigger another round of uncertainty for Malaysia's construction sector, which has benefited significantly from the influx of data centre investments, particularly in Johor and Selangor.
On Nov 20, Trump warned that American companies building data centres overseas would face a "tremendous tax" penalty, in a move aimed at strengthening the competitiveness of the US artificial intelligence (AI) sector against its Chinese rivals.
While details of the proposed restrictions remain unclear, the uncertainty could prompt data centre developers to reassess their expansion plans and postpone construction commitments until the policy's implications become clearer.
RHB Research said Malaysia's data centre contract awards had previously experienced a slowdown of about four to six months following the announcement of the proposed US AI diffusion rules in January 2025.
It said developers had adopted a wait-and-see approach amid regulatory uncertainty.
"It is not clear how Trump's foreign data centre ban would be implemented but if this policy materialises, it may renew concerns over the pace of future data centre contract awards in Malaysia for the contractors until there is greater clarity of the proposed restriction on offshore data centers," the firm said.
The firm said the implementation of such policies could create opportunities for local data centre developers, including Exsim Hospitality Bhd, Aims Group, Open DC Sdn Bhd and YTL Data Centers, as well as non-US players such as NEXTDC and AirTrunk.
It said these companies could play a key role in providing data centre leasing capacity to US technology giants that may be restricted from developing their own facilities outside the US.
"AIMS Group has given construction awards to contractors such as Binastra Corp Bhd and Gamuda Bhd, while Exsim has awarded a contract to Binastra," it added.
RHB Research said among listed construction companies, Gamuda Bhd is expected to remain resilient against the potential restrictions, supported by its diversified order book beyond data centre projects.
These include railway projects locally and overseas, renewable energy developments in Taiwan and Australia, and water infrastructure projects in Malaysia.
"With China likely pushing for self-sufficiency for chips in the long run in light of the latest US AI chip restrictions, there could be a possibility of China expanding further in other countries should US companies not be allowed to build DCs outside the US.
"As such, China may gradually grow its geographical dominance in the AI space," it added.
Despite the potential policy risks, RHB Research maintained its "Overweight" rating on the construction sector, with Gamuda, Sunway Construction Group Bhd and Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd as its top picks.

Title: Riding without helmets doubles risk of serious head injuries
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Motorcyclists and pillion riders who do not wear helmets face twice the risk of severe traumatic brain injuries in an accident
Bukit Aman's Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department warned that riding without a helmet also increased the risk of serious facial and neck injuries, which could result in permanent disability or death.
"An unprotected head faces twice the risk of severe traumatic brain injury upon impact in an accident," it said.
The department said risky behaviour among student motorcyclists was linked to disregard for traffic laws, lack of riding experience and inadequate skills. Peer pressure and a casual attitude towards road safety also contributed to accident risks.
It stressed that students must wear approved helmets correctly and comply with traffic regulations.
The department said parents played a key role in protecting children travelling to school by motorcycle.
They should ensure riders and pillion passengers wear properly fitted helmets and fasten them securely. Parents should also not allow underage children or those without valid licences to ride.
Motorcycles must have valid road tax and insurance, while brakes, tyres, lights, side mirrors and indicators should be checked before use.
Parents ferrying children to school should not exceed the permitted passenger limit or place young children in front of the rider.
All road users must obey speed limits, traffic lights and road rules, particularly near schools. They should also avoid using mobile phones, dangerous weaving and riding against traffic.
"Parents must set an example by practising safe riding habits. They should never compromise on their children's safety.
"Children's safety is not solely the responsibility of schools or enforcement authorities. It begins with the attitudes and example set by parents," it said.
Meanwhile, Road Safety Consumer Protection (PPKJR) founder and adviser Jamil Manan Supri said road safety education should be made a core subject to reduce accidents involving school students who ride motorcycles.
He said road safety education should be taught as a standalone subject rather than incorporated into other subjects such as Bahasa Melayu.
"Students must be equiped with the knowledge, skills and attitudes to become responsible road users.
"They must understand road risks, obey traffic rules and avoid behaviour that endangers themselves and others," he said when contacted recently.
Jamil said parents must ensure their children did not ride motorcycles before reaching the legal age or without a valid licence.
They should also ensure their children wore properly fitted helmets and that motorcycles were in good working condition.
He said road safety depended not only on knowing traffic rules but also on responsible behaviour and the example set by adults.
"Children learn from what they see, not just what we tell them," he said.
He called for a shift from responding to accidents to identifying and reducing risks before they occurred.
"Every child who enters the school gates must have the opportunity to return home safely.
"We cannot wait for the death toll to rise before taking action. We must not only study accidents, but also examine the systems that create the risks," he said.

Title: 18 schools in Sarawak affected by floods, but SPM unaffected
Article:
KOTA SAMARAHAN: Eighteen schools in Sarawak have been affected by floods following continuous rain during the northeast monsoon, but all 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination centres remain safe so far.
Sarawak Education director Datuk Omar Mahli said the affected schools were in the districts of Subis, Kapit, Kanowit, Miri and Sibu, with no secondary schools affected.
He said the state Education Department had nevertheless taken precautionary measures to ensure SPM candidates would not be prevented from sitting their examinations in the event of floods or road disruptions caused by bad weather.
"During the Northeast Monsoon, we cannot predict the weather, rain and so on.
"Our concern is that, in such conditions, some candidates may be left without important documents," he said during a visit to SMK Kota Samarahan in conjunction with the first day of SPM written examinations.
Omar said the Education Department was also working with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), armed forces, Malaysian Meteorological Department, Fire and Rescue Department, Civil Defence Force, Social Welfare Department and Sarawak Health Department to prepare for any eventuality.
He said school principals had also been reminded to draw on their experience of last year's floods during the SPM examinations by identifying candidates living outside school areas and ensuring they could get to their examination centres.
"If candidates do not turn up, schools must use whatever means necessary to bring them to school to sit their examinations," he said.
Candidates whose homes are severely affected by floods would be offered accommodation in school hostels to reduce the risks of daily travel and ensure they could sit all their examination papers.
"For schools without hostels, the Sarawak Education Department has identified nearby schools as alternative locations should candidates be unable to reach their original examination centres because of impassable roads or flooding.
"For example, SMK Bau is prepared to transfer candidates to SMK Lake if the school is severely affected and the access route becomes impassable. The candidates will be accommodated in a hall to sit their examinations," he said.
A total of 36,144 candidates have registered for the 2026 SPM examinations in Sarawak, which are being held at 262 centres statewide.
Of the total, 33,054 are from government schools, government-aided schools and government-aided religious schools.
Another 367 candidates are from schools under government agencies other than the Education Ministry, 983 from private schools, 1,660 private candidates and 80 from people's religious secondary schools.
Omar said 164 candidates with special needs would also sit the examinations this year, comprising 144 school candidates and the rest private candidates.
A total of 2,758 examination personnel have been appointed, including 347 volunteers, to assist in administering this year's written examinations.
Omar said the SPM examinations had begun with the Bahasa Melayu oral test from Oct 26 to 29, followed by the English oral test from Nov 2 to 5 and the Science practical tests from Nov 16 to 18, before the written papers began today.
He reminded candidates to refer to the examination timetable to ensure they observed the correct dates, times, paper codes and instructions.
They should also bring their identification documents and examination registration slips to avoid being barred from sitting the papers.

Title: Student sits for SPM despite pain after thigh surgery
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: "I am determined to sit the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination for the sake of my future," said 17-year-old Jeffry Mohammad Noor, who turned up for the written examination today despite still recovering from a road accident.
The SPM is Malaysia's national secondary school examination and an important qualification for students seeking to pursue further studies, including matriculation and pre-university programmes.
The Form Five student of Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Presint 16 (1) sat the examination in a wheelchair while still in pain.
He said the support of his parents, teachers and schoolmates had given him the strength to sit the examination.
"I have to stay strong and cannot give up because this examination is important for my future," he said when met today.
Jeffry, accompanied by his mother, Aliaa Nadiah Abdul Latif, 41, was among 243 candidates from SMK Presint 16 (1) sitting the written SPM examination today.
A total of 420,879 candidates registered for the examination at 3,334 centres nationwide.
Aliaa, a civil servant, said her son was involved in an accident with a car on Nov 13 while returning home after Friday prayers.
Jeffry was treated at Hospital Putrajaya for two weeks before undergoing surgery on his left thigh bone, she said.
She said the family had supported him throughout his treatment and encouraged him not to let the accident stand in the way of his success.
"We have always encouraged him to stay strong and face the SPM, and not to see this accident as a weakness or an obstacle to success," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 11 Malaysian companies introduce initiatives to strengthen gender equality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:
11 local organisations have introduced 31 workplace initiatives to advance gender equality, improve employee retention and create more inclusive working environments under the country's inaugural Women's Empowerment Principles Corporate Action Lab (WEPsCAL).
The initiatives, which have the potential to benefit approximately 23,000 employees, were highlighted at the 2026 Malaysia Women's Empowerment Principles (WEPs) Summit on Nov 17.
The summit also recognised local businesses through the 2026 Malaysia WEPs Awards and called on more employers to participate in the programme's second cohort, scheduled to begin in early 2027.
Launched in May 2025, WEPsCAL is the first implementation of the Corporate Action Lab model in the Asia-Pacific region.
The inaugural cohort, which ran from June 2025 to March 2026, brought together organisations from industries including aviation, manufacturing and hospitality to develop practical solutions supporting women's participation, retention and career progression.
The initiatives covered flexible working arrangements, childcare and caregiving support, fairer recruitment and retention practices, and pathways for women returning to employment.
The programme is part of the UN Women Gender Action Lab, supported by the Australian Government, and delivered through collaboration between the Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma), through Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp), UN Women and LeadWomen.
TalentCorp group chief executive officer Biruntha Mooruthi said employers had an important role in retaining experienced women and creating opportunities for them to progress in their careers.
"When experienced women leave the workforce because their workplaces cannot accommodate their circumstances, employers lose valuable skills and experience. As Malaysia prepares for changing industry needs, we must recognise the importance of retaining this talent and creating meaningful opportunities for women to grow.
"Under Kesuma's workforce development agenda, TalentCorp is working with UN Women, LeadWomen and industry partners to help employers develop practical solutions. The 31 activated initiatives from WEPsCAL demonstrate what can be achieved when companies take an active role in addressing workforce challenges. We want to build on this progress and encourage more employers to come forward," she said.
The WEPsCAL Cohort 1 Learnings Brief, presented at the summit, found that 81 per cent of participating organisations had piloted new workplace initiatives, while 69 per cent had strengthened existing policies.
United Nations resident coordinator for Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei Darussalam Nikolas Myint said advancing gender equality required collaboration between governments, businesses, civil society and development partners.
"The United Nations is pleased to stand alongside UN Women, the Government of Malaysia, the Government of Australia and private sector leaders in advancing women's economic empowerment.
"Through initiatives such as the WEPs Corporate Action Lab, companies across Malaysia are demonstrating that innovation and collaboration can help remove barriers to women's economic participation and accelerate progress towards a more inclusive, resilient and prosperous economy," he said.
Australian High Commission in Malaysia political-economic counsellor Medina Hajdarevic said the first cohort demonstrated how businesses could translate their commitments into practical action.
"Australia is proud to partner with UN Women, TalentCorp, LeadWomen and private sector leaders to advance women's economic empowerment in Malaysia.
"Malaysia's first WEPs Corporate Action Lab demonstrated how businesses can turn commitment into action, with 31 workplace initiatives activated across 11 organisations. We remain excited to support and follow the developments of the second cohort, helping companies develop practical, innovative solutions that support women's participation, retention and leadership in the workforce," she said.
The summit also marked the renewal of the memorandum of understanding between TalentCorp and UN Women Asia and the Pacific, reinforcing their collaboration on inclusive workplace practices, industry engagement and evidence-based solutions.
Meanwhile, the 2026 Malaysia WEPs Awards recognised organisations and individuals for advancing gender equality across workplaces, marketplaces and communities.
The six national winners were Allianz Malaysia Berhad for Gender-Inclusive Workplace, Messengerco for Inclusive Procurement, Oopus Organics for Community Engagement and Partnerships, UnBound Sdn Bhd for Tech and AI for Gender Equality and Mastrak Sdn Bhd for SME Champion (Gender-Inclusive Workplace).
Majidah Hashim, Head of Sustainability at Port of Tanjung Pelepas, received the Leadership Commitment Award.
Other organisations recognised as runners-up included Wipro Unza Consumer Care, Maybank, Micron Technology Malaysia, People Systems Consultancy Sdn Bhd, Axiata Group Berhad, Above Creative Events and Scubatex Resources Sdn Bhd.
Malaysia is among nine countries conducting national WEPs Awards this year, with national winners automatically shortlisted for the Asia-Pacific regional awards in December.
N Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific Gender Action Lab Regional Manager and Programme Specialist on Women's Economic Empowerment Amy Baum said the renewed partnership with TalentCorp reflected a continued commitment to translating the Women's Empowerment Principles into measurable action.
"Our renewed partnership with TalentCorp reflects our continued commitment to working with businesses to turn the Women's Empowerment Principles into concrete, measurable action.
"I warmly congratulate all the Malaysia WEPs Awardees for demonstrating what meaningful corporate leadership on gender equality looks like, and I look forward to working more closely with the awardees and other businesses in Malaysia as we seek to accelerate innovations and deliver results that promote women's full and equal economic participation," she said.
Malaysia is working towards increasing its female labour force participation rate to 60 per cent by 2030, with WEPsCAL complementing wider efforts under Kesuma to strengthen women's workforce participation and career progression.
The second WEPsCAL cohort will focus on transforming corporate ecosystems through inclusive workplaces and future-ready workplace practices, with particular attention to caregiving responsibilities, workforce diversity and changing employment needs.
Applications for the second cohort are open until Nov 30, 2026, through the programme's official
website
.

Title: Iran displays new missile technology, warns US of further 'humiliation'
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran has unveiled a new missile launcher as senior military commanders touted the Islamic republic's capabilities in defiant messages to the United States.
"A launcher capable of firing two liquid-propellant missiles simultaneously was unveiled for the first time," Iranian state television reported on Saturday.
State television broadcast footage of Revolutionary Guards chief Ahmad Vahidi and the head of the Guards' aerospace forces, Majid Mousavi, touring an underground missile base.
The two commanders were shown riding atop a vehicle through long tunnels lined with missiles, launchers and other military equipment.
"The damage suffered by our enemy is only the beginning. We shall witness their humiliation," said Vahidi, whose Revolutionary Guards form the ideological arm of Iran's military.
"Our capabilities have grown during the last two conflicts, and our high-performance weaponry can intimidate the enemy," said Mousavi.
The unveiling comes months into the Middle East war, which broke out on Feb 28 when US-Israeli strikes killed Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entered the conflict.
During the war's most intense phase, US-Israeli strikes targeted Iran's missile capabilities and again hit its nuclear sites, though the extent of the damage remains unclear.
Earlier this month, Iran unveiled a new underground missile base housing ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as launchers.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: More wardens for school hostels already in the works, says Education DG
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Education Ministry is working to increase the number of wardens at schools with hostels, with surplus teachers to be deployed to ease the workload of existing wardens.
Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad said the ministry had started appointing assistant wardens through the Malaysia Short-Term Employment Programme (MySTEP) last year and would continue the initiative this year and next.
"That planning is indeed already there at the ministry-level to ensure we have additional wardens," he said to reporters after visiting SPM candidates at SMK Putrajaya Presint 16(1).
He said teacher recruitment, which typically filled about 94 per cent of vacancies annually, had now reached 99 per cent, with some states recording a surplus of up to 103 per cent.
"So this also becomes one mechanism for us to help schools that have challenges regarding wardens," he said.
Azam said state and district education departments would coordinate the placement of surplus teachers at schools with hostels to reduce the workload of wardens.
"Our hostels here aren't just merely places to stay, not as a transit place for our children to go to school," he said.
He added that the ministry's 10,229 schools each had their own locations and challenges, and while the matter was being discussed at ministry level, any changes could not be implemented overnight.
Earlier, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek met police in Kuala Kangsar, Perak, to discuss the
safety of students
staying at a school hostel, as the ministry considers appointing more assistant wardens and guidance and counselling teachers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 304 school students killed in motorcycle crashes since 2024
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 304 school students were killed in motorcycle accidents between 2024 and August this year, with those aged 15 to 17 accounting for 235 fatalities.
Statistics from Bukit Aman's Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department  showed that 142 deaths were recorded in 2024, followed by 115 in 2025 and 47 between January and August this year.
Of the fatalities, 110 involved students aged 15 to 17 in 2024, 91 in 2025 and 34 in the first eight months of 2026.
Students aged 11 to 14 accounted for 29 deaths in 2024, 21 in 2025 and 12 between January and August this year. Another seven fatalities involved children aged seven to 10 over the same period.
In a statement, the department said 114 students suffered serious injuries and 1,443 sustained minor injuries in 2024.
In 2025, 109 students suffered serious injuries and 1,375 sustained minor injuries. Between January and August this year, 49 serious injuries and 898 minor injuries were recorded.
Students aged 15 to 17 accounted for the bulk of the injuries, with 80 serious and 1,171 minor injuries in 2024, followed by 71 serious and 1,143 minor injuries in 2025.
The group recorded 36 serious injuries and 730 minor injuries between January and August this year.
Among students aged 11 to 14, there were 27 serious and 232 minor injuries in 2024, followed by 32 serious and 197 minor injuries in 2025. A further 10 serious and 146 minor injuries were recorded in the first eight months of 2026.
Children aged seven to 10 recorded seven serious and 40 minor injuries in 2024, six serious and 35 minor injuries in 2025, and three serious and 22 minor injuries between January and August this year.
Overall, 4,322 road accidents involving school students riding motorcycles were recorded during the period — 1,704 in 2024, 1,615 in 2025 and 1,003 in the first eight months of 2026.
The department said the figures showed a downward trend in motorcycle accidents involving school students, with most occurring between 5pm and 7pm.
By road category, state roads recorded 187 accidents in 2024, 142 in 2025 and 109 between January and August this year.
Meanwhile, accidents involving students riding motorcycles without helmets resulted in 65 deaths, 50 serious injuries and 354 minor injuries in 2024.
In 2025, the figures were 53 deaths, 54 serious injuries and 335 minor injuries. Between January and August this year, 19 deaths, 23 serious injuries and 228 minor injuries were recorded.

Title: 19 Kedah schools at risk of flooding during SPM
Article:
ALOR STAR: Nineteen schools in Kedah have been identified as being at risk of flooding during the 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination due to the Northeast Monsoon.
Kedah Education Department director Azhari Abdul Rashid said precautionary measures had been taken, including preparing alternative examination centres to ensure candidates were not affected by floods.
He said the Ops Payung committee had also been activated, with emergency response plans drawn up and information on evacuation routes and nearby temporary relief centres updated.
"The schools are in Baling, Kota Setar, Pendang, Yan, Kubang Pasu and Padang Terap.
"Disaster response teams at the state education department and district education offices have also been mobilised, while emergency assets have been prepared in collaboration with relevant agencies, including the Fire and Rescue Department, National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and police.
"We are also monitoring weather conditions daily to enable swift action in the event of flooding," he said.
He was speaking at a press conference after visiting the SPM examination centre at SMK Sultanah Asma here today.
Azhari said none of the 19 schools had been affected by floods so far, although several areas had experienced rain.
He advised candidates living in low-lying and flood-prone areas to plan their journeys early and arrive at examination centres an hour before their papers began.
"Do not risk crossing flooded roads, as candidates' safety is our priority. If a route is unsafe, contact the school or district education office for assistance.
"Candidates should also keep important documents, including their identity cards, examination slips and relevant letters, in waterproof containers," he said.
Any changes to examination centres due to flooding would be announced through the official portals and social media accounts of the state and district education departments, as well as communication groups involving parents and schools.
Azhari said 30,980 candidates had registered for the 2026 SPM examination in Kedah, including 26,148 from government schools.
A total of 279 examination centres, including hospital centres, had been prepared, with 12,849 personnel assigned to ensure the smooth conduct of the examination.
He said 21 secure rooms and a security room were also operating statewide to support examination arrangements.
"All examination centres have undergone inspections covering safety, logistics, examination room management, electricity supply and technical support," he said.

Title: Alice Huang reportedly kept contact with Chinese spy agency during affair with Nvidia CEO
Article:
WASHINGTON: Alice Huang, the Chinese woman at the heart of Nvidia's recent scandal, kept in contact with an official from China's top spy agency for more than a year during her affair with former CEO Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday.
Alice Huang was in touch with an officer from China's Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the report said, citing people with knowledge of intelligence reports that describe the encounters.
A spokesman for Jensen Huang declined to comment. Representatives for Nvidia and the Chinese embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang for comment.
Alice Huang previously led Singapore-based Megaspeed International, an important Nvidia customer that once accounted for billions in Nvidia chip sales.
US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over concerns it smuggled Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China.
Sunday's report comes as US officials have cast doubt on initial suggestions that Alice Huang was a spy, as the newspaper reported last month.
That Oct 29 article touched off a scandal that led to Jensen Huang's resignation two weeks later and a steep drop in Nvidia's stock price.
Trump administration officials have repeatedly said they have not concluded that Alice Huang spied for China.
US Attorney-General Todd Blanche said this month the Justice Department had not yet reached a conclusion on whether she was a Chinese spy.
US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton repeated that on Sunday.
"Attorney General Blanche has been very clear that this is a matter under investigation, both Miss Huang and her company, for various matters," Clayton told CNN's 'State of the Union' programme. "And I'm going to let that investigation play out."
The scandal has also prompted a deeper look at Washington's approach to export controls on China, with lawmakers from both parties questioning whether the Trump administration has been too lax on enforcement and regulation of the prized semiconductors.
The affair between the two itself is of less interest, Senator John Kennedy, a Louisiana Republican, told NBC's "Meet the Press."
"I hope he had a good time," Kennedy said on Sunday. "It was the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy."--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: More than 51,000 candidates sit for SPM in Johor
Article:
PONTIAN: A total of 51,371 candidates are sitting for the 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination at 367 centres across Johor.
Johor education director Zulkurnain Abdul Rahman said 4,484 personnel had been appointed to oversee the examination.
He said this after visiting SMK Dato' Penggawa Barat here today, where he met 204 candidates and offered them words of encouragement.
Zulkurnain reminded candidates to bring their identification documents and examination registration statements to their centres, and comply with all examination rules and procedures.
He said the Education Ministry had put in place an integrated response mechanism with security and health agencies to safeguard candidates and examination personnel.
At SMK Dato' Penggawa Barat, three examination rooms were operating, with another three quarantine rooms prepared for candidates showing symptoms of fever or infectious diseases.

Title: 965 SPM candidates in Kelantan face flood risk
Article:
KOTA BARU: Fourteen Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination centres involving 965 candidates in Kelantan have been identified as being at risk of flooding.
Kelantan Education Department director Siti Norina Muhamad said Pasir Mas recorded the highest number, with nine examination centres, followed by Machang and Tumpat with two each, and Kuala Krai with one.
She said eight of the centres were in areas where both access routes to examination centres and candidates' homes could be affected by floods.
"The remaining six are in areas where only roads leading to examination centres are inundated, while the centres themselves and candidates' homes remain unaffected.
"The department has prepared contingency plans through close cooperation with security agencies, including the armed forces, police, Fire and Rescue Department and Civil Defence Force, to ensure candidates can reach their examination centres.
"We have also made alternative arrangements by providing hostel accommodation for SPM candidates in the event of flooding in their respective areas," she told reporters here after visiting SMK Kota Bharu in conjunction with the first day of the SPM examinations.
Siti Norina said a total of 27,998 candidates were sitting the 2026 SPM written examinations at 298 centres across Kelantan, which began today.
She said all logistical, security and welfare preparations were at an optimal level to ensure the examinations proceeded smoothly without disruption.
A total of 3,248 examination personnel had been appointed to ensure the smooth conduct of this year's SPM, while Ops Payung had also been activated as a precaution against possible disasters or adverse weather throughout the examination period.
"The Examinations Board has also provided special arrangements for 398 candidates with special needs, including extra time, separate examination rooms and enlarged-print or Braille examination papers," she said.

Title: SPM candidates in flood-prone areas to be housed in school hostels
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates in flood-prone areas will be placed at schools with hostel facilities to ensure their examinations are not disrupted.
Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad said the Education Ministry had identified areas frequently affected by floods and sought parents' consent to place candidates in nearby hostels, where meals would be provided free throughout the examination period.
"We have identified villages that frequently experience floods and roads that could be cut off, preventing our candidates from reaching school.
"We have arranged for these students to be placed at nearby centres with hostel facilities so their examinations will not be disrupted," he told reporters after visiting SPM candidates at SMK Putrajaya Presint 16(1) today.
Azam said the ministry had also held meetings with other agencies, including the armed forces, police and Civil Defence Force, to coordinate emergency responses, as floods could affect areas not previously expected to be hit.
"For unexpected situations, we will manage," he said, adding that authorities would help candidates cross flooded roads or arrange alternative transport to examination centres when necessary.
He cited previous instances of members of the public offering vehicles, including lorries and heavy machinery, to ferry candidates through flooded areas, describing the efforts as an example of community solidarity.
"Actually, that is our society's nature — always supporting our children sitting for examinations," he said.
Azam said the ministry would continue monitoring the situation with schools and other agencies throughout the examination period.
A total of 420,898 candidates are registered for the 2026 SPM examination, with the written papers beginning today and running until Dec 17.

Title: 18 months after Putra Heights blast, dozens of homes remain unrepaired
Article:
SUBANG JAYA: Eighteen months after the Putra Heights gas pipeline explosion, dozens of homes in Taman Putra Harmoni remain damaged, forcing some residents to continue living elsewhere.
A check found homes near the blast site still bearing damage to roofs and fences from the intense heat, which reached 1,000 degrees Celsius
Many damaged houses remain vacant, with their owners reportedly renting elsewhere or staying with relatives.
The prolonged delay has raised questions over the progress of negotiations between affected residents and the authorities, with no mutually acceptable settlement reached so far.
This is particularly so for 36 residents who filed a civil suit against five parties, including Petronas Gas Bhd (PGB) and the government, at the Shah Alam High Court in October last year.
Residents' representative Loh Poh Heng said the case was proceeding through the courts, with trial scheduled for July next year.
He said the homes had yet to be repaired because government aid came with conditions requiring residents to sign documents waiving their right to pursue further legal action.
"We are still renting or staying elsewhere while waiting for a resolution. We hope a fair settlement can be reached for all affected residents," he said when contacted.
He said all 36 families remained committed to pursuing the civil suit to seek justice.
Loh said the residents were seeking compensation for losses involving their homes, health and emotional well-being, as well as justice and transparency from the authorities.
Another resident, who wished to be known as Adi, said many homes near the blast site remained unrepaired since he returned to the neighbourhood last year.
"I understand some residents took their cases to court because they disagreed with the compensation offered, resulting in delays to the repair process.
"However, some homes have been repaired and their owners returned towards the end of last year," he said.
Adi said his house was not badly affected as it was some distance from the explosion site.
"My house suffered minor roof damage, which has since been repaired. The belongings and appliances inside were also intact," he said.
A check at the explosion site found that the crater left by the fire had been filled in.
In July last year, PGB announced that it had completed the gas-in process for a newly constructed bypass pipeline on July 1, 2025, restoring full gas supply to key areas in Batu Tiga, Shah Alam and Connaught Bridge.
Repair works were also ongoing at shop lots beside the explosion site.
The gas pipeline fire on April 1 last year destroyed 81 homes, while another 81 suffered damage exceeding 40 per cent. A further 57 homes were affected but not burnt, while 218 others were undamaged.
A total of 399 vehicles were also affected, including 225 that were destroyed and 174 that sustained partial damage.
A parliamentary Special Select Committee on Infrastructure, Transport and Communications report tabled in the Dewan Rakyat in October last year concluded that the Putra Heights incident resulted from a combination of environmental, technical and poorly controlled local development factors.
Although no sabotage or operational negligence was found, the report highlighted weaknesses in development controls and the need for continuous monitoring of critical infrastructure.

Title: AI boom drives Malaysia exports to record RM1.81tril, SMEs contribute RM63.6bil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's exports rose 37.1 per cent year-on-year to hit RM1.81 trillion in the first 10 months of 2026, fuelled by the global artificial intelligence (AI) investment boom and stronger demand for electrical and electronics (E&E) products.
The growth, the strongest for the January-October period since 1990, lifted the country's trade surplus to RM274.81 billion, already exceeding the highest surplus recorded in any full year since 1990, the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) said.
Beyond the record figures, the performance also highlights the growing contribution of Malaysian small and medium enterprises (SMEs), which are expanding their presence in international markets and diversifying beyond traditional export industries.
E&E shipments jumped 53.9 per cent to RM891.99 billion, reflecting Malaysia's position in global technology supply chains amid rising demand for semiconductors and AI-related infrastructure.
Non-E&E exports also recorded strong growth, rising 24 per cent to RM919.17 billion and generating a trade surplus of RM74.03 billion.
Among SMEs that participated in Matrade's international trade programmes, 7,434 companies collectively generated RM63.60 billion in exports, supported more than 383,000 jobs and recorded a trade surplus of RM12.04 billion.
Significantly, 7,211 of these companies contributed RM57.29 billion in non-E&E exports, accounting for about 90 per cent of their combined export value.
Their participation spanned a broad range of industries, including processed food, chemicals, machinery, equipment and parts, metal manufactures and palm oil-based manufactured products.
Matrade chief executive officer Datuk Indera Abu Bakar Yusof said the record export performance demonstrated the ability of Malaysian companies to compete in global markets, but expanding SME participation remained a key priority.
"Our historic export figures prove that Malaysian enterprises are formidable players in the global value chain, but our core mission now is aggressively expanding the SME slice of the export cake," he said.
He said the RM63.60 billion in exports generated by the 7,434 SMEs engaged with Matrade demonstrated the impact of the agency's trade promotion initiatives.
Meanwhile, exports to non-traditional markets, including Africa, Central Asia and Latin America, rose 23.7 per cent to RM80.57 billion during the 10-month period compared with the corresponding period last year.
Several markets recorded particularly strong growth, led by Namibia, where exports surged 470.2 per cent, followed by Libya (399.8 per cent), Tanzania (47.5 per cent), Brazil (40 per cent), Ethiopia (36.4 per cent) and Angola (27.7 per cent).
Other markets registering increases included Puerto Rico, Algeria, Kenya, Uzbekistan and Egypt.
The expansion into these markets reflects the growing importance of geographical diversification in strengthening Malaysia's trade resilience, particularly as businesses navigate supply chain disruptions, geopolitical uncertainty and changing demand patterns.
Looking ahead, Matrade is strategically recalibrating its initiatives to align with the progressive targets of the 2027 Budget and the 13th Malaysia Plan, with greater emphasis on helping SMEs expand internationally, strengthen their capabilities and comply with environmental, social and governance (ESG) requirements.
"To sustain this momentum amid global uncertainty, we will deepen the market diversification strategy by expanding engagement with non-traditional markets and promoting higher value-added products.
"This proactive recalibration is crucial to broadening our export base, reducing reliance on traditional markets, and engineering long-term trade resilience," Abu Bakar said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 73,594 Selangor SPM candidates receive food baskets, lunch aid
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A total of 73,594 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates under the Selangor Education Department will receive food assistance and nutritious meals under the 2026 Selangor Nutrition Programme (Nutrisel).
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said RM3 million had been allocated for the programme, comprising RM2.9 million from the State Economic Planning Unit and RM100,000 from Menteri Besar Incorporated (MBI) through Yayasan MBI.
He said 71,152 candidates from 256 schools, including national secondary schools (SMK), religious secondary schools (SAM and SAMT), Chinese independent secondary schools (SMPC), special model schools and private tahfiz schools, would receive nutritious lunch sets.
"Each candidate will receive a nutritious lunch worth RM8 a day for five days of core subject examinations," he said to reporters after officiating the Nutrisel SPM handover ceremony at Maahad Integrasi Tahfiz Selangor Alam Impian.
Meanwhile, 2,442 candidates from 20 schools and institutions, including boarding schools (SBP), integrated boarding schools (SBPI), national religious secondary schools (SMKA), Selangor Integrated Tahfiz Maahad (MITS), MARA Junior Science Colleges (MRSM) and special education institutions such as Kolej Permata@Pintar, will receive Nutrisel food baskets.
Amirudin said the baskets contained vitamin C, bread, cereal, milk, chocolate and student essentials such as water tumblers and hand-held fans.
He said 66 candidates, comprising 50 MITS students and 16 private candidates, received the food baskets this morning.
He also presented RM50,000 in assistance for repairs to MITS Alam Impian's prayer room and sports facilities as part of the state government's efforts to improve amenities for the community.
Asked about SPM candidates in Selangor affected by floods, Amirudin said he had yet to receive any fresh reports.
"The education department is already aware of the situation following my earlier visit. We will arrange transportation and other assistance to ensure they can travel to and from their examination centres.
"During my visit to SK Binjai in Meru recently, two to three SPM candidates were affected. The situation has improved so far.
"The floodwaters in Parit Mahang, Kuala Selangor, have also begun to recede. We will look into helping them with the cleaning up of their homes," he said.

Title: Translating ICJ's historic judgment into tangible justice for the Rohingya
Article:
LETTER:
Last Thursday, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in its judgment in The Gambia v. Myanmar, found that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya population in northern Rakhine State during the 2017 military clearance operations.
For the first time, the principal judicial organ of the United Nations expressly determined that a State had committed genocide.
The more difficult question is whether this judicial recognition can be translated into meaningful accountability, reparation and protection for the Rohingya people.
By finding that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the Court reinforced a fundamental principle: the prohibition of genocide is not merely a prohibition addressed to individuals.
It also generates binding obligations for States, including the obligation not to commit genocide, to prevent it, and to punish those responsible.
Perhaps the most legally significant aspect of the judgment concerns the establishment of genocidal intent, or 'dolus specialis.'
The Court examined the totality of the evidence, including the historical discrimination against the Rohingya, the systematic deprivation of citizenship and other fundamental rights, anti-Rohingya hate speech, the targeting of villages, killings, sexual violence, attacks against children, forced displacement and the destruction of settlements.
Importantly, the Court did not treat these incidents as isolated violations. It assessed their cumulative significance, their systematic character and their relationship to the broader pattern of conduct directed against the Rohingya population.
Particularly important is the Court's recognition of the right of displaced Rohingya to safe, voluntary and dignified return, together with family reunification, the restoration of property and rehabilitation for victims.
The Court also found that Myanmar had violated its obligation under the provisional measures order of Jan 23, 2020 to preserve evidence relevant to allegations of genocide.
[[nid:1583632]]
The displacement of Rohingya communities has raised serious humanitarian, migration, protection and regional security concerns across Southeast Asia.
Although Asean's principles of non-interference and consensus-based decision-making present institutional challenges, they should not be interpreted as requiring regional silence in the face of genocide.
The objective should not be to transform Asean into a judicial institution, but to ensure that regional diplomacy does not become an obstacle to international accountability.
The true measure of this judgment lies not in the legal principles it establishes or the historical significance of its findings, but in the tangible difference it makes to the lives of the Rohingya people.
It must be reflected in their ability to return to their homes in safety and dignity, regain their citizenship and fundamental rights, reunite with their families, obtain adequate reparation for the suffering they have endured, and see those responsible held accountable.
For the international community, the message is unmistakable: the prohibition of genocide must amount to more than a solemn commitment proclaimed in 1948.
It must function as a living and enforceable obligation, capable of protecting vulnerable populations and ensuring that States are held accountable when they breach it.
The central question, therefore, is no longer whether international law recognises genocide as one of the gravest crimes.
It is whether the international community possesses the political will to translate that recognition into genuine accountability and lasting justice.
DR MOHAMMED R. M. Elshobake
Assistant Professor

Title: HI Mobility bags RM666mil contract for 23 Johor bus routes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Local and cross-border bus operator HI Mobility Bhd has secured an RM665.68 million contract to operate 23 bus routes across Johor Bahru and its surrounding areas for five years under the Stage Bus Service Transformation programme.
Its wholly-owned subsidiary, Handal Indah Sdn Bhd, received the letter of acceptance from the Land Public Transport Agency (Apad) for the appointment as the intracity bus service network operator.
The contract runs from 2027 to 2031, covering a network of long buses, electric buses and minibuses to cater for passenger demand and expand connectivity across the city.
The routes will connect residential communities with key commercial, retail and institutional destinations, including Mid Valley Southkey, Toppen Shopping Centre and Universiti Teknologi Malaysia.
The contract comes amid the broader transformation of Johor Baru's public transport landscape, particularly with the upcoming Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link connecting Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru to Woodlands North in Singapore.
Its executive director and chief executive officer Lim Chern Chuen said the company was grateful to Apad for the confidence placed in it through the appointment.
"As Johor Baru's public transport network continues to evolve, particularly with the introduction of the RTS Link, the integration of different modes of transportation will become increasingly important in connecting commuters to their destinations," he said in a statement.
The bus network is expected to complement the RTS Link by providing first- and last-mile connectivity, linking residential areas and communities to rail stations and other destinations.
The integration of bus and rail services will strengthen intermodal connectivity, while the deployment of electric buses will support greener public transportation in Johor.
